It is significant as it shows Morphy's strength outside his characteristic open games and contributed to his reputation as America's first chess champion.

positions.tournament: First American Chess Congress, New York
positions.significance: This game was played in the final match of the 1857 American Chess Congress, Morphy's breakthrough tournament. Paulsen, one of the world's best defenders, held Morphy to a draw in a tense, strategic battle using the then-rare Sicilian Defense. The game is significant as one of the few draws in Morphy's career, showing his ability to handle positional play and resistance in high-stakes settings.

The game is significant as one of the few draws in Morphy's career, showing his ability to handle positional play and resistance in high-stakes settings.
